title: Invoicing step: editable date, Confirm dates, certificates, skippable
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in with View and edit customers, on the build under test. The Maintenance Reminders feature is on (maintenance_reminders flag).
  2. A service is due or overdue on an enrolled asset (e.g. 'PM-A' on unit 'ZZAUTOTEST Truck 12').
custom_steps:
1. In the step after invoicing, confirm the proposed date is editable and names the day the work was done, with next due following it.
  2. Use Confirm dates to accept every proposal in one action; confirm closing the step without touching it accepts every proposal too.
  3. Confirm a Compliance certificates section appears for every compliance service on the work order.
  4. Confirm the step appears only where a maintenance service was completed, never on an ordinary work order, and nothing blocks closing the work order.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The proposed date is editable and names the day the work was done; the next due follows from it and updates as it changes.
  • Confirm dates accepts every proposed date in one action; closing the step without touching it accepts every proposal too, and the step is skippable (nothing blocks closing the work order).
  • The step carries a Compliance certificates section for every compliance service on the work order (one record per inspection: type, number, Start date, End date and term), and it is optional.
  • The step appears only where a maintenance service was completed; it never appears on an ordinary work order.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780 (Maintenance Reminders); story SV-10574 (S18, Complete a service and reset the cycle); Chunk 2 MR spec (Confluence 897679389), Part 1 / S18; read 2 Oct 2026. Source-verified 2 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S18-R13: “Where a work order added the lines of one or more maintenance services, invoicing it shows each of those services with the date its cycle counts from. The date proposed is when that service's own lines were all closed, which S18-R9 stamps, and the invoice date only where there is nothing better. Every path that closes a line stamps that date: completing the line, the bulk action bar, creating an invoice, clocking out and review. Where a path leaves no date, the invoice date is proposed”
  • S18-R14: “The proposed date is editable and names the day the work was done. The next due follows from it through the service's own interval and updates as it changes, so a shop invoicing weeks late resets from the work rather than from the paperwork”
  • S18-R15: “Accepting every proposed date is one action, Confirm dates. A shop that invoices on the day of the work passes through without touching it, and closing the step without touching it accepts every proposal too, per S18-N5”
  • S18-R16: “The same step carries a Compliance certificates section for every compliance service on this work order, one record per inspection: type, number, Start date, End date and term, where Start date plus the term fills End date per S8-R10. The section is optional”
  • S18-N5: “The step appears only where a maintenance service was completed. It never appears on an ordinary work order, and leaving without touching it accepts every proposal, on the same rule as S18-N1”
  • S18-N6: “Completing a work order shows no maintenance step. Everything happens in the step after invoicing”
  • S18-N1: “The completion step is skippable. Nothing blocks closing a work order”

AUTOMATION: HOLD - not yet build-verified on a Maintenance Reminders QA build (feature ships behind the maintenance_reminders flag)
